title: Perspective: A Principled Framework for Pliable and Secure Speculation in Operating Systems
problem: Transient execution attacks can leak entire memory contents from operating system kernels through speculative execution gadgets. The OS is particularly vulnerable because kernel-level gadgets can access sensitive data across the entire system.
motivation: Protecting operating systems from transient execution attacks is exceptionally challenging yet critical, as kernel compromise exposes all system memory.
method: Perspective adds two mechanisms to the Linux kernel (tested using gem5 hardware simulation). Data Speculation Views (DSVs) enforce data ownership: they prevent the CPU from accessing data speculatively (guessing ahead) unless the current execution context (the user or task running) owns it. Instruction Speculation Views (ISVs) restrict which kernel functions the CPU can speculatively execute per execution context and block load instructions (memory fetch operations) from running speculatively in unauthorized functions.
key_novelty: Instruction Speculation Views enable fine-grained control (per execution context—per user or task) over which kernel functions the CPU can execute speculatively (guess what instructions to run), enabling swift patching of attack gadgets and reducing the passive attack surface (vulnerable execution paths attackers can exploit without injecting new code).
contributions: Taxonomy of transient execution attacks in OS kernel distinguishing active attacks (self-exploitation) from passive attacks (victim coercion)
Data Speculation Views mechanism to enforce data ownership and prevent unauthorized speculative access
Instruction Speculation Views mechanism to whitelist executable kernel functions speculatively per context
Linux kernel implementation with 3.5% overhead on microbenchmarks and 1.2% on datacenter applications

metrics.other: 3.5% execution overhead on microbenchmarks, 1.2% on datacenter applications

limitations: The abstract does not discuss specific limitations of the approach.
primary_theme: Defending OS kernels from transient execution attacks
